3SG absolutive: tu-ke; 3SG ergative: tu-ra. All 3rd person forms (sg, dl, pl, proximal) have ergative counterparts with -ra.

Main clauses consistently show ergative marking on A NPs and pronouns. This is the primary domain of the ergative pattern.

All dependent clause types (non-finite and finite) show ergative case marking on A arguments, with the exception of general purpose clauses where A receives genitive marking (still an ergative-based system). No S/O pivot found in dependent clauses.

Guillaume explicitly concludes there is NO split ergativity in Cavineña morphology. The apparent split reported by Camp (1985) is due to a morpho-phonological rule of suffix deletion (-ra and -ke deletion), not a morpho-syntactic split. At the syntactic level, co-reference constraints in dependent clauses operate on a NOMINATIVE-ACCUSATIVE basis (S/A pivot), not ergative.

The ergative marker =ra (NPs) / -ra (pronouns) is DISTINCT from the genitive marker -ja (e.g. e-kwe 'my', tata-chi=ja 'father's'). In general purpose dependent clauses, A receives genitive marking -ja, but this is a distinct morpheme from the ergative =ra.

The ergative marker =ra is distinct from instrumental and comitative markers. No syncretism between ergative and instrumental/comitative reported for Cavineña (contrast with Panoan languages like Matses/SK where -n marks ERG=GEN=INST).
